key_insight: Mimir is a physics-grounded LLM irrigation agent that improves long-horizon control by pairing fast, simulator-verified action repair with slow accumulation of persistent contextual principles.
engineering_relevance: The work shows how to safely combine LLM reasoning with deterministic physical constraints for real-world control systems where errors compound over time.
method: LLM proposes irrigation actions through a structured physical interface.
A deterministic simulator numerically checks, revises, and bounds actions before execution.
Recurring failures are distilled into persistent context, while the physical model and constraints stay fixed.
evidence_signal: Across multiple sites, crops, and years under a common retrospective evaluator, Mimir achieved the lowest reported aggregate control cost and used about 51% less irrigation than historical schedule replay.
watch_item: Performance depends on the fidelity of the simulator and evaluator, so mismatches between modeled and real soil-water dynamics could limit deployment robustness.
paper_title: Mimir: Physics-Grounded LLM Agents for Long-Horizon Irrigation Control
